title: THC Cultivation Foundations Certificate
publicDescription: This draft THC Academy certificate candidate is designed to recognize successful completion of the Cultivation Foundations curriculum and demonstrated foundational knowledge across twelve cultivation domains. It emphasizes evidence-based reasoning, measurements with units, traceable records, source-aware interpretation, and the ability to distinguish direct observation from unsupported conclusions. The credential is not authorized for certification use until the human-review, accessibility, pilot, standard-setting, and release-approval gates recorded in this definition are complete.
intendedAudience: Entry-level cultivation technicians and cultivation support staff
Learners preparing for more advanced THC Academy cultivation coursework
Adult learners seeking a structured, evidence-based foundation in cannabis cultivation science

assessmentModel.knowledgeAssessment: The configured Foundations final is a randomized 60-item summative assessment sampling five scored items from each of twelve competencies. Production use requires a reviewed active item pool and the repository's separate assessment-integrity controls.
assessmentModel.retakePolicy: The configured final permits up to three attempts with a 24-hour cooldown so remediation can occur before another scored attempt. These settings remain subject to evidence-based review before certification use.
assessmentModel.completionEvidence: The candidate eligibility model requires completion of the credentialed course version plus a passing result on the configured Foundations final. Formative lesson or module activity alone is not credential evidence.
assessmentModel.performanceEvidence: No separate occupational performance assessment is currently required by this foundational certificate candidate. Hands-on occupational performance is assessed more extensively in technician-level pathways.

employmentUse: After release authorization, the certificate may serve as evidence of structured foundational cultivation education for entry-level hiring, onboarding, or internal development decisions.
After release authorization, it may serve as prerequisite knowledge evidence for progression into more advanced THC Academy pathways.
It does not independently authorize regulated work, replace employer qualification, or establish government licensure.
